subject.title: fix(update): dev channel update builds from an unverified checkout at the git install path

question: Should package-to-dev conversion permanently refuse every pre-existing `OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR`, accepting migration friction to eliminate checkout-adoption risk?
rationale: The security direction is strong, but the hard refusal intentionally breaks a previously supported conversion workflow and repository policy requires explicit ownership of that compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: Approve fresh-path-only conversion
options.body: Keep unconditional refusal of existing paths after the clone boundary and current-head retry flow are hardened and proven.

options.title: Design explicit adoption mode
options.body: Preserve an owner-approved opt-in adoption workflow only if it can establish a comparably strong trust boundary with clear warnings and upgrade coverage.

recommendation.title: Approve fresh-path-only conversion
recommendation.body: Keep unconditional refusal of existing paths after the clone boundary and current-head retry flow are hardened and proven.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history places this contributor closest to the updater orchestration and compatibility surface.
